Start here: Harmonizing data with beFAIR

K.A. Stam

2026-11-13

Source: vignettes/start_here.Rmd
start_here.Rmd

What is beFAIR?

Running a multi-study research platform means dealing with data in different formats, naming conventions, and structures across studies. beFAIR solves this by providing a shared, codebook-driven framework for collecting and harmonizing clinical research data into a single SQL database — following the FAIR data principles.

FAIR stands for:

  • Findable — data and metadata are easy to discover
  • Accessible — data can be retrieved with standard protocols
  • Interoperable — data uses shared vocabularies and formats
  • Reusable — data is well-described and can be reused across studies

beFAIR achieves this by combining a codebook-driven schema with auto-generated ETL scripts. Every table in the database is defined by a codebook (a YAML file specifying variable names, types, and validation rules). Scripts are drafted automatically, leaving you to fill in only the study-specific data mapping logic.

The three data pillars

A FAIRground is organized around three data pillars:

Study

studies/

Clinical trial metadata — participants, study arms, scheduled events, and the ID mapping that links source identifiers to anonymised participant IDs.

Experiment

experiments/

Laboratory measurements on participant samples — e.g. CyTOF, ELISA, Olink, and flow cytometry.

Analysis

analyses/

Processed or derived results computed from study and experimental data.

Each pillar lives in its own subdirectory and contains one or more ETL scripts alongside a meta.yaml describing the dataset and a data/ folder pointing to raw source files.

The codebook system

Every database table is defined by a codebook — a YAML file that describes each variable: its name, data type, allowed categories, and validation rules. Codebooks are the shared vocabulary that makes data comparable across studies.

Here is an example for the age variable in the participant codebook:

age:
  description: Age of subject at enrollment; in years. Usually an integer, but
    decimals are allowed for newborns (e.g. 0.2).
  units: years
  type: numeric
  type_sql: DECIMAL
  categories: ~
  labels: ~
  validations:
    - col_is_numeric: []
    - col_vals_between:
        left: 0
        right: 120
        na_pass: true
        label: "Age in years should fall within specified range"

beFAIR ships with built-in codebooks covering all standard study, experiment, and analysis tables. For assays or schemas unique to your project, you can also place custom YAML codebooks in the codebooks/ folder inside your beFAIR project directory — they are treated identically to built-in ones. See the Codebook configuration guide to learn how to read, write, and add custom codebooks, and the Codebook reference for the full list of available built-in codebooks and their variables.

How beFAIR works

Depending on your role, beFAIR will mean something different to you.

I want to use data from the database

The database is already populated and you want to query or retrieve data. Connect using FAIRgroundConnect() with your DSN, then use standard DBI calls to read tables.

FAIRgroundConnect("MY_DSN")
con <- FAIRgroundConnection()

DBI::dbReadTable(con, "participant")

A DSN (Data Source Name) is an ODBC connection string configured by your database administrator. For local testing without a server, see the Database smoke test.

To pull all tables related to a specific study, experiment, or analysis ID — following relationships across all three pillars — use collectTablesById():

collectTablesById(id = "CHSI1")   # returns a named list of all linked tables

See the Database smoke test for a worked example of connecting and querying the database.

I want to add data by writing ETL scripts

A FAIRground directory already exists and you need to contribute data for a new study, experiment, or analysis.

FAIRgroundConnect("MY_DSN")

addStudy("MyStudy", study_id = "MYST1")       # scaffolds scripts under studies/
addExperiment("MyStudy_CyTOF_exvivo",
              experiment_type = "CyTOF")       # scaffolds scripts under experiments/
addAnalysis("MyStudy_CyTOF_clustering")        # scaffolds scripts under analyses/

Each function drafts the required ETL scripts for you. Your job is to fill in the data-mapping logic. See Adding a study, Adding an experiment, and Adding an analysis for step-by-step walkthroughs.

I am a developer or database maintainer

You are responsible for keeping the database up to date — running ETL scripts, managing codebook versions, and onboarding new contributors.

Day-to-day: re-run any new or changed scripts and reload the database:

FAIRgroundConnect("MY_DSN")
databaseUpdate()

First-time setup: create the project directory and initialize the database:

startProject(dir = "/path/to/my/project")
FAIRgroundConnect("MY_DSN")
databaseInitialize()

databaseUpdate() is the main orchestrator — it syncs codebook definitions, detects new or changed scripts, runs each one, validates the output, and loads it into the database. Start with Starting a project for the full setup walkthrough, and Developer internals for a deep dive into databaseUpdate() and the registry tables.
